summary.headline: Radiant Cash Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin fell to 7.62% from 15.2% as manpower costs rose; management guides to 12-14% price hikes lifting margins from Q4.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs 1.12 billion, up 4.4% YoY, while standalone revenue grew 7.52%. Standalone EBITDA margin compressed sharply to 7.62% from 15.2% a year earlier, driven by higher manpower costs (minimum wages in some states, shortage of licensed gunmen in southern states), which make up about 70% of costs. Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 6.8% from 13.1%, with the fintech subsidiary Radiant Ace Money reaching near breakeven. Management said price increases negotiated with banks will feed through from Q3 and more fully from Q4.

financial_highlights.change: vs 18.4% in Q1 and 15.7% a year ago

financial_highlights.value: About 80 days revenue as of September 2026
financial_highlights.change: Rose in September; management says it was a timing effect, collected in October

segments.name: Retail cash management (core)
segments.commentary: Grew 6.2% YoY; driven by BFSI and organised retail, with e-commerce logistics recovering. Cash handled was flat at about Rs 0.41 trillion (transcript figure; analyst referenced about Rs 1.6 lakh crore annually). Serviced 79,374 points across 15,165 pin codes and 9,217 locations, up about 5% YoY.

segments.name: Radiant Ace Money (fintech subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew on sound box orders and BC-network transactions; near breakeven EBITDA in the quarter after PIDF subsidy ended in December 2025. Deployed 21,000 sound boxes and facilitated about Rs 200 crore transaction volume; network of about 20,000 BCs. MoUs signed with two small finance banks, one urban bank and some NBFCs.

segments.name: Radiant Valuable Logistics
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 29.9 million, up 35% QoQ; management targets positive EBITDA in the current fiscal year. Still loss-making and a drag on margins.

guidance_outlook: Price increases of roughly 12-14% secured mainly from banks; impact expected from Q3 and fuller from Q4 FY27 as contracts reprice, with implementation targeted by December.
Management declined to give an exact standalone margin target; an analyst's 20-21% framing was not confirmed, but management said the improvement will be significant.
Subsidiary losses in Radiant Valuable Logistics and Ace Money expected to narrow and turn positive contribution to EBITDA in the current fiscal year.
Technology-led cost reduction programme underway, targeting manpower costs (about 70% of total cost).
Management expects top-line growth to improve through direct clients and hiring sector specialists; past 5-7% growth described as not sustainable.
capex_capacity: Capex is minimal; most vehicles and premises are taken on lease, per management.
Ace Money had some capex on sound boxes, described as self-liquidating inventory purchases rather than material capex.
Points serviced rose about 5% YoY to 79,374; management estimates about 45% share of the industry's cash-in-transit points (industry under 2 lakh points).
demand_pricing: Price hikes of 12-14% were negotiated, mostly with banks; pricing for direct clients is the same mechanism as for banks.
No fuel cost pass-through exists in contracts.
Cash volumes grew more slowly than management would like; cash handled is flat YoY and per-point volumes are declining marginally.
Direct clients are about 20% of revenue; management is hiring industry specialists to win e-commerce, organised retail and other direct accounts.
Management said the industry leader's margin gap could not be compared; peers faced similar wage and cost issues.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins far below the industry leader's mid-20s when costs are similar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it lacks comparable data on peers; said pricing to banks is similar across providers and all peers raised the same manpower cost concern with the industry association and the Indian Banks Association.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 12-14% price hike lift standalone margin from about 8% to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give an exact number because bank start dates differ; said there will be a definite significant improvement, with impact visible from Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price hike applicable to retail and bank contracts, and is guard shortage easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Most hikes came from banks. Gunman shortages persist in specific states, mainly north, east and southern regions; alternatives being explored; no immediate impact from the Agniveer tenure change.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company consider a share buyback instead of dividends given net cash above Rs 150 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the suggestion without committing; the questioner argued buyback would be tax-efficient for the promoter, a point not addressed by management.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price hike plus loss reduction be enough to restore margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management listed four levers: price hikes (largest), narrowing losses in the two new ventures, technology-led cost cuts, and direct-client growth; each to add a few percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Will the receivables increase persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the September receivables spike was a one-time timing effect; October collections were good and the balance was collected in the first week of October.

risks_watch: Standalone EBITDA margin recovery depends on the timing and extent of bank price hikes from Q3-Q4 FY27; the 7.62% Q2 margin is well below the prior-year 15.2%.
Manpower cost inflation from minimum wages and licensed gunman shortages in several states could absorb price gains.
Flat cash volumes and muted growth (6.2% retail) versus management's ambitions; direct-client share is still about 20%.
Losses in Radiant Valuable Logistics and Ace Money are still a drag; delivery of breakeven/positive EBITDA in this fiscal year is unproven.
Receivables at about 80 days need to normalise; the September spike is attributed to timing.
Cash-volume impact from upcoming state elections was raised by an analyst but not answered.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the price-hike pipeline and cost programme, but evasive on peer comparisons and on quantifying the margin path. Management repeatedly deferred specific numbers, citing differing bank start dates.
key_quotes: Radiant Ace Money has had good growth in the revenues during this quarter aided by healthy orders for sound box deployment, steady growth and transaction revenues from the existing BC network.
The management expects healthy improvement in profitability on account of core business profitability improvement supported by the recent price increase price hike from the customers.

growth.why: Management guides to a definite significant margin recovery from 12-14% price hikes negotiated mainly with banks, impact from Q3 and fuller from Q4 FY27, and subsidiary losses narrowing to positive EBITDA this fiscal; no explicit revenue growth target given, with past 5-7% growth called unsustainable and cash handled flat YoY, so top-line outlook stays flat.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 7.62% from 15.2% on manpower costs (about 70% of cost); 12-14% price hikes negotiated mainly with banks take effect from Q3 and fully from Q4, with management calling the improvement significant but not quantifying it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capex is minimal with vehicles and premises leased, and points serviced rose only about 5% YoY to 79,374, so no new capacity is signalled in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Cash handled is flat at about Rs 0.41 trillion YoY, per-point volumes are declining marginally, and retail grew only 6.2%; management itself calls the 5-7% past growth unsustainable without a stated target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is minimal and assets are leased, and utilisation was not discussed, so no capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No explicit revenue or margin guidance was given and management declined to quantify the margin path, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Price-hike start dates differ across banks and manpower inflation plus gunman shortages could absorb gains, while the 7.62% margin sits far below last year's 15.2%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Not discussed beyond Ace Money's sound-box deployments of 21,000 units, which are existing rather than new launches.

rows.label: Subsidiaries reach positive EBITDA this fiscal
rows.why: Radiant Valuable Logistics revenue rose 35% QoQ to Rs 29.9 million and still loses money, while Ace Money is near breakeven after the PIDF subsidy ended in December 2025; management targets positive EBITDA but has not proven it.

rows.label: Bank price hikes of 12-14% repricing contracts
rows.why: Price increases of 12-14% were secured mainly from banks, with implementation targeted by December and fuller impact from Q4 FY27; no fuel pass-through exists in contracts.

rows.label: Technology-led manpower cost reduction
rows.why: Manpower is about 70% of total cost and a technology-led programme is underway, but no savings figure was given and gunman shortages persist in several states.
